algorithms.name: Saving a chapters version
steps: Take the proposed chapters, the author (manager or agent name), who asked (operator or none), the reason, and whether the save was asked for.
Every citation must resolve: Hub record ids against the project's tables, commit shas and tag names against the project's repository. Any that does not resolve refuses the whole version, naming it.

Every surface knot of the structural thread that existed when the previous version was saved must sit in exactly one chapter; a missing or doubled knot refuses the version, naming it. Knots recorded since may be placed or left ungrouped.

If the save was not asked for, compare each existing chapter with the proposal: any change to its title, summary or members is dropped and named in the result; only new chapters are kept. If nothing new is left, no version is written.
Write the version as a new row; never update or delete an earlier one.

algorithms.name: A chapters firing
steps: Skip if the job is off; skip an automatic trigger if the job is button-only.

Gather the structural surface (slice 1's feed), the current chapters with every earlier version and its reason, and, if no chapter yet covers the time before the first Hub record, a digest of the repository's history before it: release tags with their dates and the subjects of the commits between them.
Spawn the job's runner and model once with that input; record the firing with its usage whatever the outcome.
Save the answer through 'Saving a chapters version' with author manager, asked-for when the trigger was the button.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-25: 'the agent should use the mock. It should look exactly like that'.
requirements.statement: The Thread page renders as the approved mock (hub/ui/mock-loom.html, left to right, wave) renders the same knots: the same thread shape, knot spacing and sizes, labels, header line, panel layout, typography, colours in dark and light, and motion; the only differences allowed are agents' registered colours and what real data adds (paging, live knots).

requirements.rationale: The operator chose left to right on 2026-10-24. Even spacing keeps knots from a busy few days legible beside months-long chapters.
requirements.statement: The Thread page lays the project's surface knots on one thread from left (oldest) to right (newest), evenly spaced in time order; opening the page selects the newest surface knot with it in view, and two controls select the first surface knot and the newest one.

requirements.rationale: A straight line with dots read as a git graph; the wave is the operator's chosen thread.
requirements.statement: The thread is drawn in madder as a smooth wave that passes through each knot, alternately above and below the middle, swinging further for knots that hold more; each knot carries its date or date span and its title on the side away from the middle; and where 10 or more days pass between two neighbouring knots the thread is labelled with that silence ('3 weeks later', '2 months later').

Above the thread the page states how many chapters the project has, the span of days they cover, and how many newer surface knots are not yet in a chapter; with no chapters it states the number of surface knots instead.

requirements.rationale: The operator asked for more information under the thread about the selected knot, 'whatever we can show'.
requirements.statement: Beneath the thread a panel describes the one selected knot: its kind as glyph and word with its position among the knots of that kind beside it ('Chapter 17 of 17'); its title; its summary when it has one; when it happened and how long it lasted; how many knots it holds directly and all the way down; who was in it, as named chips in each agent's registered colour, including the actors of what it holds; what it is made of, as a count per kind; a control that opens the object it stands for; and controls for the knot before and after it.

When the selected knot holds others, the panel shows them as a smaller thread of the same kind; choosing one selects it, the panel then describes it and shows a trail naming every knot above it, each of which selects that knot again; when the selected knot holds nothing, the smaller thread shows the knots beside it with it marked.

requirements.rationale: Chapter spans are stored as whole UTC days; read as instants they move a day east of UTC (seen in the mock).
requirements.statement: A chapter's dates are shown as the calendar days the manager wrote, in any time zone: a chapter written for 24 October shows 'Oct 24' and '1 day', never 'Oct 24 – Oct 25' or '23h 59m'.

requirements.rationale: Carries pull-the-thread FR-12 into the horizontal layout, where an Earlier/Later button at the end of a list no longer fits.
requirements.statement: A thread, surface or inner, whose loaded knots do not reach the beginning or the present loads the next page on that side when the reader scrolls within one screen width of that end, without changing the selected knot or moving the knots already in view; for a project with 10,000 recorded items the first knots show within one second of opening the page and any page loads within one second.

requirements.rationale: Carries pull-the-thread FR-10: links to a knot keep working after the redesign.
requirements.statement: Selecting a knot puts its address in the URL; opening a knot's address selects that knot with the trail of every knot above it, brings it into view in the panel's thread and on the surface, and gives it keyboard focus.

requirements.rationale: Carries pull-the-thread FR-11.
requirements.statement: Activity recorded while the page is open appears at the present end of the surface thread, and in the panel when it belongs to the selected knot, within five seconds without a reload, and does not change the selected knot or move the view when the reader is elsewhere on the thread.

With a knot focused, Left and Right select and focus the knot before and after it, Home and End the first and last loaded knot, Enter on a knot that holds others selects the first knot it holds, and Escape selects the knot above; a vertical mouse wheel over a thread scrolls it sideways, and pressing and dragging a thread pulls it along without selecting the knot the drag started on.

requirements.rationale: The operator asked for more animation and polish, and accepted the mock's motion.
requirements.statement: On opening, and whenever a thread is shown afresh, the thread draws in from its oldest end and each knot appears as the thread reaches it; a glint passes along the thread after it is drawn and then about every 14 seconds; the selected knot is tied with a loop and gently pulses; choosing a knot glides it into view; and the panel's contents rise in as the selection changes. Under reduced-motion settings none of this moves and the page shows the same content.

While the chapters job is on, the page offers 'Weave the thread' as it does today; a page that cannot be read says so and asks for a reload, and a part that cannot be read says so without hiding what did load.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: the manager decides what grouping best represents the work, whether by time, theme or roadmap; once chapters exist they stay shown.
requirements.statement: When a project has chapters, the Thread surface shows them ordered by when each begins, each with a title, a plain-language summary, its time span and who wrote it; opening a chapter shows, in place, the knots it groups. A project with no chapters shows slice 1's structural surface.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23.
requirements.statement: Chapters may overlap in time, so that two themes built in the same weeks are two chapters whose spans intersect.

requirements.rationale: Chapters are a reading of the history, not a filter on it; an item a chapter drops appears to the reader as if it never happened.
requirements.statement: Every surface knot of slice 1 belongs to exactly one chapter, so opening every chapter reaches the same items as the structural thread, none twice and none missing; a knot recorded after the latest chapter version appears after the chapters, ungrouped, until a later version places it. A chapter version that would drop or duplicate a knot is refused.

requirements.rationale: The roadmap's done-condition: chapters cite only real records. The page's promise is that nothing appears out of thin air.
requirements.statement: Every record a chapter cites (a stored Hub record, or a commit or tag in the project's repository) exists when the chapter is saved; a chapter version with any citation that does not resolve is refused and the previous version stays shown.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: this project's imported history is distilled from git, and its commits are shown grouped. Here that is 5,382 commits from 2026-03-07, 91 release tags and 221 dated archived openspec changes.
requirements.statement: For history earlier than the project's first Hub record, the manager writes chapters distilled from the project's git history, placed at the dates of the commits they cite and before every Hub-recorded knot. Opening one shows its commits grouped by the release tag they shipped in, each commit with its date, author and subject.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: these events are enough for now.
requirements.statement: With the chapters job enabled and automatic firing on, it fires after each major event in the project: a specification document approved, a document archived, or the last task of a document approved. It also fires whenever the operator presses 'Weave the thread' on the Thread page.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: a user who does not want this, or wants it done only by hand with a specific agent, must be able to say so.
requirements.statement: The operator can, per project: leave the chapters job off (the default), turn it on with automatic firing, or turn it on for the 'Weave the thread' button only; and choose which runner and model it uses. With the job off, the button is absent and nothing fires, and an agent the operator asks can still write chapters through its tools.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: no cost cap; control and visibility instead. The first firing over a long git history is the expensive one.
requirements.statement: Each chapters firing records what it cost (tokens and, where the runner reports it, money) and the operator can see the cost of each firing and the project's total for the job.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: rewriting is allowed but avoided unless the user asked, so the story a reader saw yesterday is still there today. The Hub enforces it rather than trusting the model to obey.
requirements.statement: A firing the operator did not ask for only adds chapters for knots no chapter yet holds; any change it proposes to an existing chapter is refused and the existing chapter stays as it was. Existing chapters are rewritten only by a firing the operator asked for, or by an agent a user asked to.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: future runs must know how the thread changed. Shown to agents only, for now.
requirements.statement: Every change to a project's chapters is kept as a new version recording who made it (the manager or a named agent), who asked for it when anyone did, when, and why; no earlier version is lost, and each firing and each agent reading chapters is given the earlier versions and their reasons.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: a user can ask an agent to organise the view as they like, using git commits or anything else the agent can read.
requirements.statement: An agent can read a project's chapters and their versions, and can create, retitle, resummarise, regroup or remove chapters through its tools; each edit is subject to citations-resolve and every-knot-once, and is recorded as a version under the agent's name.
Every project offers a tab labelled Thread, placed immediately after Overview, that shows that project's thread and nothing from any other project.

requirements.rationale: One thread for the whole project: an item missing from it is history that appears out of thin air.
requirements.statement: Every recorded item of these kinds appears beneath exactly one surface knot: specification documents and their phase changes; tasks and their status changes; runs; evidence and its review verdicts; merges into main; questions and their answers; permission decisions; messages between agents; job and loop firings; operator conversations; vault additions.

At the surface, each specification document is one knot placed at its first recorded activity; items belonging to no document are surface knots of their own, and consecutive such knots with no document knot between them are folded into one knot naming their count and time span.

Every knot shows, without being opened: its kind as a glyph and a word, a plain-language title, its date or time span, the names of who acted, and how many knots it holds when it holds any. No raw identifiers or event-type names appear on the face.
Every knot that stands for a stored object (document, task, run, evidence, conversation, job firing, vault entry) links to that object's existing view in the app.

requirements.rationale: The page's whole claim is traceability; an invented or misplaced knot breaks it for every reader.
requirements.statement: Every knot corresponds to stored records and is placed by their recorded time; the thread never shows an item that has no stored record, and never reorders items against their recorded times.

Within any thread, four or more consecutive knots of the same routine kind (runs, status changes, messages, firings) are shown as one folded knot naming the kind and count, which opens to show them individually; milestone knots (document approved, evidence accepted, merge) are never folded.

For a project with 10,000 recorded items, the tab shows its first knots within one second of opening on the operator's machine, and moving to the beginning or opening any knot shows its contents within one second; scrolling never waits for the whole history to load.
